subject: Capacity gap analysis and staged remedial plan for private GPU pools

From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, EdgeCloud Ops <ops@edgecloud.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity gap analysis and staged remedial plan for private GPU pools

Team / EdgeCloud ops,

I ran the Q3 sizing delta against our expected run rates and there is a material shortfall for the private GPU pools serving the 8:00–12:00 PST burst window. Summary:

- Sustained throughput target: 25k completion tokens/min across tenant lanes (target SLO).
- Current provisioned headroom (per recent telemetry): ~15k tokens/min.
- Gap: ~10k tokens/min (≈ 6 rtx-80xx-equivalent GPUs depending on quantization profile).

Attached: gap_analysis_q3.xlsx (calc tab + assumptions) and a 20-minute capture of the worst-case network traces we saw last week (network_traces.zip). Key asks:

1) Jonas / Karthik — can you confirm the preferred fallback routing (region vs model-variant) when we hit the top-of-pool queue? I want to ensure the remediation doesn't rely on behavior that's not routable in the private environment.
2) EdgeCloud ops — what is the earliest lead time for a temporary bridge allocation (4 GPUs) in the us-west-2 onprem cluster?
3) Marissa / Laura — we need procurement and legal input on a short-term capacity OLA and any required onboarding for a third-party bridge.

Proposal (short-form): staged remedial plan spanning 6 weeks — short bridge + kernel/quantization switch for hot paths + KV cache warmup tweaks. If that sounds reasonable I'll sketch a timeline. Please reply with availability for a 30-min sync this afternoon.

Thanks,

Chloe Martin
Principal Cloud Architect — Inference
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, EdgeCloud Ops <ops@edgecloud.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity gap analysis and staged remedial plan for private GPU pools

Chloe — thanks for the write-up and attachments. Quick notes:

> - Gap: ~10k tokens/min (≈ 6 rtx-80xx-equivalent GPUs depending on quantization profile).

Can we tighten the estimate by splitting the gap into two components: sustained baseline load (steady QPS) and transient amplification (burst multiplier)? From the trace the transient multiplier looks like 2.2x for 90s windows. If the steady-state gap is smaller we may avoid provisioning the full 6 GPUs and instead rely on burst admission + prioritized KV cache warmup.

About fallback routing: the private deployment supports two viable fallbacks in order of preference: 1) intra-region fallback to a compatible quantized model on spare slabs, 2) cross-region failover to hosted Redwood (where permitted). We need to lock in route 1 as the primary; route 2 has compliance gating for some accounts.

I'm going to open INF-723 and attach a trimmed simulation showing steady vs burst sizing. Linking it here: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-723

Jonas
Senior Infrastructure PM

Chloe / team — appreciate the quick analysis. High-level signoff for a staged approach: short bridge + software mitigations + infra rightsizing. A few operational constraints before we proceed:

- Procurement needs an unambiguous runbook for onboarding any third-party capacity (IDs, network ACL changes, compliance checklist).
- Any bridge allocation must include a defined eviction window and traffic-shaping rules so we can remove it with minimal tenant impact.
- We should prioritize a software-first path that reduces the delta by ~30% (quantization/kernel changes + aggressive cache priming) while the bridge is a temporary buffer.

Please prepare a 6-week timeline with owners and acceptance criteria. Marissa — can you produce the draft OLA + estimated cost delta? Chloe / Jonas — I'll need a short one-pager (pdf) that lays out the remedial timeline and acceptance criteria for exec review; attach as staged_remediation_timeline.pdf.

I'll block 30 minutes at 1:30pm PT for a triage sync.

Laura Bennett
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Hi all — Ops here (EdgeCloud.ai). Quick response on availability and constraints:

- We can provision a temporary bridge of up to 4 rtx-80xx-equivalent GPUs in us-west-2 within 48–72 hours, subject to signed OLA and network ACL updates. Lead time to reach 6 GPUs is ~14 days.
- Network change notes: we will require the following from Redwood before we push changes to the private fabric: 1) a CIDR list for ingress sources, 2) SSH key for bootstrap, 3) clear egress rules (we cannot permit cross-region egress without explicit compliance approval).
- Cost estimate (ballpark): 4 GPUs / 6 weeks = $XX,XXX (final quote will follow once procurement confirms PO terms).
